record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does there exist a countable dense homogeneous metric space that is not Polish?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Does there exist a CDH metric space that is not Polish?
Both Problems 6 and 6’ were solved in the affirmative by Farah, Hrušák and Martínez Ranero [25].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A separable metric space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $A, B \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ such that $h(A) = B$. A topological space is called Polish if it is separable and admits a complete metric compatible with its topology.

Question: Does there exist a countable dense homogeneous metric space that is not Polish? That is, can one construct a separable metrizable space $X$ which is CDH but which is not homeomorphic to any complete separable metric space?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively by Farah, Hrušák, and Martínez Ranero, who constructed a CDH metric subspace of the real line that is not Polish (in fact, a non-Borel CDH subset of the reals exists in ZFC).

status_evidence.title: A countable dense homogeneous set of reals of size aleph_1
status_evidence.snippet: Farah, Hrušák, and Martínez Ranero construct in ZFC a countable dense homogeneous subspace of the real line of size aleph_1, which is therefore not Polish.
status_evidence.claim: There exists a CDH metric space that is not Polish.
